claims.text: The starting PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles are homogeneous solid-solution high-entropy alloys with uniformly distributed metal atoms.
Lowering the cyclic-voltammetry upper potential limit suppresses transient oxidation of Rh sites.
Lowering the cyclic-voltammetry upper potential limit suppresses transient oxidation of Ru sites.
Transient oxidation of Rh and Ru produces surface oxy-species.
Oxidation of alloy constituents can induce structural transformation under electrocatalytic conditions.
Rh- and Ru-derived oxy-species trigger irreversible surface restructuring in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Transient oxidation of Rh and Ru causes metal dissolution from PtPdRhRuIrOs.
A conventional high upper potential limit causes more extensive transient oxidation of Rh and Ru than a lowered upper potential limit.
Reducing Rh and Ru oxidation by lowering the upper potential limit preserves catalyst structure.
Preserving the catalyst structure and reducing metal loss improves long-term durability during ethanol oxidation.
The lowered-upper-potential protocol will produce a lower metal-dissolution rate than the conventional protocol.
The lowered-upper-potential protocol will produce less surface restructuring than the conventional protocol.
The lowered-upper-potential protocol will improve durability over extended cycling.
Initial ethanol-oxidation activity will remain similar after lowering the upper potential limit.
There is a potential window that drives ethanol oxidation while limiting excessive Rh- and Ru-derived oxy-species.
The proposed mechanism applies in acidic electrolyte at room temperature.
In situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy can track oxidation-associated catalyst transformations under electrochemical operating conditions.
